subject: Re: AstraMed private deployment — VPC/on-prem activation Q&A and preflight
body:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@astramed.health>

Cc: Network Ops <netops@astramed.health>, Joelle Park <joelle.park@astramed.health>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AstraMed private deployment — network diagram and quick checklist

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare for the activation window on Jun 3, the network team asked for a short, actionable preflight checklist and the final network diagram so we can validate firewall/policy changes and schedule a maintenance window with our data center.

Could you confirm the following items for the private (VPC + on-prem peering) deployment?
- Do you require inbound ports from our jump host to Redwood management endpoints (IP ranges)?
- NAT/egress expectations for telemetry and KV-cache replication?
- TLS mutual-auth details (client cert fingerprint) and KMS access pattern for envelope keys?
- Any additional firewall rules for telemetry/export agents (ports and FQDNs)?

I attached our local network diagram and a skeleton checklist. We can provide a traceroute and sample pings during the test window if that helps.

Attachments: astramed-local-diagram-v1.pdf (application/pdf), astramed-preflight-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks —

Head of Infrastructure
AstraMed Health

On Thu, May 21, 2026 at 10:02 AM irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:

Subject: Re: AstraMed private deployment — network diagram and quick checklist

Alex — great questions, thanks for sending the diagram.

Short answers up front so your ops team can proceed this week: 
- Management plane: we do require outbound connectivity from your environment to our management endpoints. We do not need inbound ports opened to customer infra. We will provide a CIDR list (regional) for egress allowlist; expected connection pattern is HTTPS (443) with mutual TLS for control-plane calls.
- Egress: telemetry and KV-sync will originate from our private nodes; for on-prem peering we expect customers to allow outbound to our telemetry endpoints on 443 and to a small set of S3-compatible object stores for snapshot uploads (we'll enumerate FQDNs).
- TLS/mTLS & KMS: we'll use customer-managed KMS for data encryption at rest via envelope keys. We need a service account and a limited IAM role that permits Encrypt/Decrypt/WrapKey for the envelope operations. We will share the client cert fingerprint and expected CN pattern.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound 443 to telemetry.redwood.ai and management.redwood.ai (regional endpoints) and allow NTP (UDP 123) to avoid clock drift on certs. No additional inbound ports required unless you want an optional SSH jumpbox for debug during the activation window (we prefer ephemeral bastions).

I've attached a focused preflight checklist and our network diagram (v2) that includes CIDR hints and expected ports. Please circulate to NetOps.

Attachments: astramed-network-diagram-v2.pdf (application/pdf), sccm-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Next steps: once you confirm the allowlist entries we will schedule a short verification run (30–45 minutes) during the Jun 3 activation slot. If NetOps needs a traceroute or sample pings we can coordinate a 15-minute call the day before.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Looping in Vivek for the ops/infra runbook details and Kim for the account setup bits. A couple of internal notes for the activation plan: 

- Vivek: we need a concise list of CIDRs we will publish to AstraMed (regional by AZ). Can you confirm whether we should provide a /24 per region or a tighter prefix? Also list of FQDNs for telemetry and snapshot object store.
- Kim: confirm required IAM permissions for the KMS service account on AstraMed side (we asked for Encrypt/Decrypt/WrapKey only). Also confirm if we should request a separate service-account for audit-only access (read-only) for log pulls.

Irene — after you hear back from NetOps, let's produce a one-page operational runbook (30–45 min verification steps + rollback checklist) and attach to the HubSpot deal. We should also ask for a signed MOP for the maintenance window if their change control requires it.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

On Mon, May 25, 2026 at 09:26:00 -0700 vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AstraMed private deployment — network diagram and quick checklist

Quick infra notes (drafted for the one-pager):
- Published egress: we'll provide three /28 blocks per region for control-plane and telemetry (keeps BGP/NAT trivial and small surface area). If customer CI/CD needs static egress, we can consider separate /24 on request but prefer smaller allocations.
- Ports/FQDNs: outbound TCP/443 to management.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com (for snapshoting) and object-store.astramed.backups (if they run privately). UDP/123 for NTP.
- mTLS: client certs issued by our CA; we'll send cert fingerprint and CN format. Root rotation plan included in runbook.
- KMS: require role: redwood-encrypt-service (minimal perms: kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt for env keys). Recommend customer enable key policy to allow cross-account decrypt by the service account.
- Debug access: ephemeral AWS Systems Manager session manager preferred over opening SSH. If Nebula on-prem we request a jumpbox IP for the day of activation (time-limited).

I'll turn this into a one-page MOP and link it back. Irene/Kim — any regulatory specifics AstraMed flagged we should call out (PHI-handling, logging retention)?

-Vivek
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Alex / Joelle —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are the items Vivek and I finalized: the concise activation MOP (one page), the updated network diagram (v2) with annotated CIDRs, and the KMS IAM role template. We also listed a minimal acceptance checklist for SOC/SCCM items you flagged.

Would you please confirm the following by Tues, Jun 1 so we can lock the Jun 3 activation at 02:00–04:00 PT?
1) Confirm acceptance of the three /28 egress blocks per region (we included candidate IPs in the diagram).
2) Confirm an IAM role name to attach the Encrypt/Decrypt permissions (we've suggested redwood-encrypt-service).
3) Confirm whether NetOps will allow outbound access to s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com for snapshot uploads or provide an internal object-store FQDN.

If all good we'll post the MOP to the HubSpot deal and request your change approval. For the activation we'll run: network verify (15m), cert handshake and KMS test (10m), KV sync smoke (10m), perf sanity (10m). Rollback steps included.

Attachments: astramed-network-diagram-v2.pdf, sccm-acceptance-checklist.xlsx, redwood-kms-role-template.txt

Best,
